review_notes: I read the whole file. I did not open the related sources, so this verdict rests on the file's own text and its imports. The new declarations are specific to the graded path algebra. They are the vertex simple (a specialisation of the generic `gradedPositiveMulQuotient`), the quotient map, the arrow morphism, the arrow sum (an `abbrev` over the existing `GradedModuleCat.directSumObj` and `shiftObj`), the short complex (a plain `ShortComplex.mk`), the simplicity and exhaustiveness results, and the class basis (an instantiation of `gradedIdempotentHeadBasis`). Each one reuses existing Mathlib or library machinery such as `ShortComplex`, `ShortExact`, `HasProjectiveDimensionLT`, `Projective`, `Simple` and `Module.Basis`. None of them is a competing independent version of an existing concept. The named wrappers (`gradedVertexSimple`, `gradedArrowSum`) are deliberate specialisations whose docstrings explain their role. I found no case for consolidation. The only uncertainty is that I did not search the TauCeti sources for earlier duplicates inside the library.
